idle.title: Press Start to watch a package travel from code to a running system
idle.plain: Every safety check you will see is real. The left side is the process. The bottom is the machinery doing the work. They light up together.
idle.technical: Start creates a Tekton PipelineRun in namespace sdlc-build. Each BPMN task maps to a TaskRun and its pod; the cluster view is a live read of the Kubernetes API.

done.title: A signed, scanned package is stored and verified
done.plain: Now try to run it. Deploy the signed package, then try to break the rules with an unsigned one.
done.technical: The pipeline finished: image pushed by digest, SBOM generated, scan gate passed, image signed and SBOM attested with Cosign, signature re-verified.

start.title: A developer saves a change
start.plain: Someone on the team saves new code. This starts the journey.
start.technical: In a full setup a git push would trigger the pipeline. In this demo the Start button creates the PipelineRun.

commit.title: A developer saves a change
commit.plain: Someone on the team saves new code. This starts the journey.
commit.technical: In a full setup a git push would trigger the pipeline. In this demo the Start button creates the PipelineRun.

build.title: Packing the software into a sealed box
build.plain: The code is packed into a container image: a sealed box with everything the program needs. The box gets a fingerprint, so any later change can be spotted.
build.technical: Buildah builds the image in-cluster (no Docker daemon) and pushes it to Harbor. Harbor returns the digest (sha256) that identifies it.

sbom.title: Listing every ingredient
sbom.plain: A tool opens the box and writes down every part inside. This parts list is called an SBOM, a Software Bill of Materials, like an ingredient label.
sbom.technical: Syft reads the image from Harbor and writes an SPDX-JSON SBOM into the shared workspace.

scan.title: Checking the parts for known problems
scan.plain: The parts list is compared with a public list of known weaknesses, like checking food for a recall.
scan.technical: Trivy scans the SBOM against its vulnerability database and fails the task if any CRITICAL finding exists.

gw1.title: Is anything critical?
gw1.plain: If a serious known weakness is found, the build stops here and goes back to the developer. Nothing unsafe moves forward.
gw1.technical: Gate: trivy --severity CRITICAL --exit-code 1. A non-zero exit fails the PipelineRun, so the signing step never runs.

reject.title: Stopped: fix and try again
reject.plain: A serious problem was found, so the package was stopped before it could be approved.
reject.technical: scan task failed; sign-attest and verify are skipped.

sign.title: Putting a tamper seal on the box
sign.plain: The package passes, so it gets a digital seal. If anyone changes it afterwards, the seal no longer matches. The ingredient list is sealed to it too.
sign.technical: Cosign signs the image digest with the lab's private key (held only as a cluster Secret) and attaches the signed SBOM attestation next to the image in Harbor.

store.title: Filing it safely and double-checking
store.plain: The warehouse keeps the box, its ingredient list and its seal together. The pipeline then checks the seal once more.
store.technical: Harbor stores image + signature + attestation. The verify task runs cosign verify and verify-attestation with the public key.

req.title: Someone asks to run it
req.plain: Now somebody asks the cluster to start the program. Before it agrees, the security guard looks at the box.
req.technical: A Pod create request reaches the Kubernetes API in namespace sdlc-apps; the Kyverno admission webhooks evaluate it.

gw2.title: Is the seal intact?
gw2.plain: The guard checks two things: does the seal match, and does the box come from our own warehouse. If not, the answer is no.
gw2.technical: ImageValidatingPolicy verifies the Cosign signature and SBOM attestation against the public key; ValidatingPolicy requires harbor.local:9443/poc/.

ok.title: Allowed: the program runs
ok.plain: The seal was good, so the cluster started the program. Trust was checked, not assumed.
ok.technical: Admission allowed; the pod was pulled from Harbor (node trusts the lab CA) and started.

blocked.title: Blocked: the cluster says no
blocked.plain: No valid seal, or the wrong source, so the cluster refused to run it. This is the whole point: bad packages are stopped at the door.
blocked.technical: The admission webhook denied the request. The message below is Kyverno's real answer.

sdlc-build.blurb: Where each step of this build runs, one short-lived worker (pod) per step.

harbor.blurb: Stores the packages, their ingredient lists and their seals.

tekton-pipelines.blurb: Starts a worker for each step and keeps the order.

projectcontour.blurb: Lets traffic in to reach the warehouse safely over HTTPS.

kyverno.blurb: Checks every request to run a program and says yes or no.

cert-manager.blurb: Issues the certificates that make connections trusted.

sdlc-apps.blurb: The only place the guard's rules apply in this demo.
